The [[UEFA Europa League]], formerly the UEFA Cup, is an [[association football]] competition established in 1971 by [[UEFA]].<ref name="rsssf">{{Cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/ec3b.html |title=UEFA Cup/Europa League |publisher=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=1 June 2023}}</ref> It is considered the second most important international competition for European clubs, after the [[UEFA Champions League]]. Clubs qualify for the Europa League based on their performance in national leagues and cup competitions. For the first 25 years of the competition, the final was contested over [[Two-legged match|two legs]], one at each participating club's stadium, but in 1998, [[Inter Milan]] defeated [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] in the competition's first single-legged final held at a neutral venue, the [[Parc des Princes]] in Paris.<ref>{{cite web |title=1997/98 season history |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/history/seasons/1997/ |date=31 May 2008 |publisher=UEFA |access-date=13 May 2020 |archive-date=2 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201202031151/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/history/seasons/1997/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] won the [[1971–72 UEFA Cup|inaugural competition in 1972]], defeating [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] 3–2 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/uefacup/history/season=1971/intro.html |title=Spurs keep Wolves at bay |publisher=UEFA |date=2 January 2006 |access-date=29 June 2008 |archive-date=20 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120320051306/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/index.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Eleven finals have featured teams from the same national association: Italy ([[1990 UEFA Cup final|1990]], [[1991 UEFA Cup final|1991]], [[1995 UEFA Cup final|1995]] and [[1998 UEFA Cup final|1998]]), England ([[1972 UEFA Cup final|1972]], [[2019 UEFA Europa League final|2019]] and [[2025 UEFA Europa League final|2025]]), Spain ([[2007 UEFA Cup final|2007]] and [[2012 UEFA Europa League final|2012]]), Germany ([[1980 UEFA Cup final|1980]]) and Portugal ([[2011 UEFA Europa League final|2011]]).

[[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] holds the record for the most victories, having won the competition seven times since its inception.<ref>{{cite web |title=Europa League kings Sevilla beat Roma on penalties to win seventh crown |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/sevilla-beat-roma-4-1-penalties-win-seventh-europa-league-title-2023-05-31/ |website=Reuters |access-date=1 June 2023 |date=1 June 2023}}</ref> [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] (winners in [[1985 UEFA Cup final|1985]] and [[1986 UEFA Cup final|1986]]) and Sevilla (winners in [[2006 UEFA Cup final|2006]] and 2007, and [[2014 UEFA Europa League final|2014]], [[2015 UEFA Europa League final|2015]] and [[2016 UEFA Europa League final|2016]]) are the only teams to have retained their title. The competition has been won fourteen times by teams from Spain, more than any other country.<ref name="rsssf"/> The last champions before the UEFA Cup was renamed to UEFA Europa League were [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]], who beat [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] 2–1 after extra time in the [[2009 UEFA Cup final|2009 final]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/may/20/shakhtar-donetsk-uefa-cup-werder|title=Shakhtar Donetsk claim Uefa Cup final glory over Werder Bremen|date=21 May 2009|work=The Guardian|access-date=11 August 2009}}</ref> [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] and [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] have lost the most finals, with three losses in the competition. The current champions are [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], who defeated [[SC Freiburg]] 3–0 in the [[2026 UEFA Europa League final|2026 final]].

While the [[Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]] is considered to be the predecessor to the UEFA Cup, UEFA does not recognise the Fairs Cup as one of its official club competitions, and therefore its records are not included in the list.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.uefa.com/uefa/news/kind=1/newsid=2571.html |title=UEFA Cup: All-time finals |date=30 June 2005 |access-date=15 March 2008 |publisher=UEFA |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080309094213/http://www.uefa.com/uefa/news/kind%3D1/newsid%3D2571.html |archive-date=9 March 2008}}</ref>
